 Alabama Crimson Tide TUSCALOOSA, Ala.— No. 18 Alabama is back in Coleman Coliseum for the fourth game of its five-game opening home stand, and it is the first high-major opponent of the season as the Seton Hall Pirates come to Tuscaloosa. 
--> TUSCALOOSA, Ala.— No. 18 Alabama is back in Coleman Coliseum for the fourth game of its five-game opening home stand, and it is the first high-major opponent of the season as the Seton Hall Pirates come to Tuscaloosa. 
 Here's all the info you need for Alabama's fourth game of the season.

 Latest Injury News for Seton Hall at Alabama 
--> Latest Injury News for Seton Hall at Alabama 
 There will be no official pregame availability report since this is a non-conference matchup, but Alabama head coach Nate Oats said during his Thursday press conference that sophomore forward Jamarion Davis-Fleming would be unlikely to play in Friday night's game as he has not been practicing throughout the week.

 Fleming is in street clothes for pregame warmups and will not play.

--> When :   Friday, Nov. 13, 8 p.m. CT
 Where :   Coleman Coliseum, Tuscaloosa, Alabama
--> Where :   Coleman Coliseum, Tuscaloosa, Alabama
 All-Time Series : Tied 1-1 with the first matchup occurring on March 13, 2001.
--> All-Time Series : Tied 1-1 with the first matchup occurring on March 13, 2001.
 Officials : Bart Lenox, Chuck Jones, Matt Potter
--> Officials : Bart Lenox, Chuck Jones, Matt Potter
 Last Meeting : The Pirates beat Alabama 83-78 on Nov. 19, 2010, in the U.S. Virgin Islands. Trevor Releford and Senario Hillman combined for 38 points, but it wasn't enough. Tony Mitchell logged 13 points, as he and Chris Hines were responsible for 20 of Alabama's 38 rebounds. The Tide held a 5-point lead at halftime, but the Pirates outscored UA by 10 in the second period. Jeremy Hazell scored 27 points for Seton Hall, with three other starters also finishing in double figures.
